There, along his primary meridian, it encountered the obstruction the System had detected.
The clearing process was mercifully gentle.
There was no unbearable agony.
No violent explosion of energy.
No dramatic shattering of invisible chains.
The Liquid Qi simply dissolved the blockage as effortlessly as water dissolved salt.
Over the span of barely ten seconds, the obstruction melted away completely.
The pathway opened.
For the first time since obtaining the System...
His meridians were complete.
For the first time in his life, his body could draw ambient Qi from the world around him.
Everything changed.
It was as though he had spent his entire life blind, only to suddenly open his eyes.
He could feel it.
The countless streams of Qi flowing through the air.
The lingering spiritual essence permeating the cave.
Even though the Spirit Pool had vanished, the cave still contained an astonishing concentration of ambient Qi, far denser than anywhere else he had ever encountered.
And for the first time...
He could truly sense it.
Taking a deep breath, Stan instinctively drew in the Qi surrounding him.
The moment the energy entered his body, an indescribable sense of exhilaration washed over him.
’So this is what cultivation feels like...
It’s intoxicating.’
The sensation made him wonder what it would be like in a place where Qi was almost nonexistent.
The Introduction to Earth had described Earth’s environment as being nearly devoid of spiritual energy.
Compared to this cave, it would probably feel like trying to breathe through a blocked nose.
Here, however, he could clearly sense the lingering Qi left behind by the vanished Spirit Pool.
Even though the treasure itself had disappeared, traces of its spiritual essence still permeated the cave, slowly leaking into the surrounding glacier.
He absorbed as much of it as he could.
Then he noticed Camilla.
She, too, was cultivating.
The ambient Qi rushed toward her with astonishing speed, spiraling around her body like a massive vortex before disappearing into her meridians.
Stan’s eyes widened.
At the rate she was absorbing it, the remaining Qi inside the cave would probably be completely exhausted within an hour or two.
’Royal Blood vampires are monsters...’ Just then, another notification appeared before him.
[Meridian clearing complete.]
[Host is now officially classified as a cultivator.]
[Current Realm: Genesis Realm, Initial Stage.]
Stan slowly let out a breath he hadn’t realized he was holding.
He was finally...
A cultivator.
Beside him, Camilla frowned.
Her crimson eyes fixed themselves on him, carefully examining the aura now radiating from his body with the practiced instincts of a Royal Blood.
’Impossible...
A moment ago, he didn’t possess the slightest trace of Qi.
Now...
He’s emitting the aura of an Initial Stage Genesis Realm cultivator.’
’What in the world is he...?’
’How did he?’
She had barely formed the thought when Stan suddenly vanished.
Not into the mysterious treasure she believed he possessed, as one would think...
He simply...
Disappeared.
The sensation was similar to the last time he had vanished when the werewolf attempted to sever his spine.
Yet this time, it felt fundamentally different.
Stan hadn’t activated nor willed anything.
He felt as though an invisible hand had suddenly seized him before violently pulling him sideways through space itself.
The icy cave blurred into streaks of distorted light.
Reality twisted around him.
He had no time to react.
No time to resist.
No time even to comprehend what was happening.
It happened too fast...
He was first blinded by darkness.
Then all he could see was blinding white.
Then...
The world reassembled itself.
An instant later, he found himself standing somewhere entirely unfamiliar.
Back inside the cave, Camilla stared at the empty space where he had stood only moments earlier.
Her crimson eyes narrowed.
Then, to her own surprise, she smiled.
A faint, amused smile tugged at the corners of her lips as she gently shook her head. ’Did he think I would kill him now?’
’That life-saving treasure again...’
’So he can use it multiple times.’
She let out a quiet chuckle.
"How curious."
"Why is someone who’s supposedly just a mortal so much more intriguing than the true humans I’ve met?"
Naturally, she had mistaken his disappearance for another use of that mysterious treasure.
There was no conceivable way for her to know that Stan hadn’t entered any storage space this time.
Nor could she know that he had been forcibly teleported, dragged away by an external force he neither understood nor controlled.
Her gaze drifted toward the empty cavity where the Spirit Pool had once rested.
She sighed softly.
"How long can you hide inside that treasure of yours?" she murmured, more to herself than anyone else.
"I’ll wait."
"Whenever you decide to come out...
I’ll still be here."
A dangerous glint flashed through her crimson eyes.
"If I truly want you..."
"...there’s nowhere you can hide from me."
With graceful elegance, she sat upon a protruding ledge of ice overlooking the empty basin.
She folded her hands neatly in her lap and settled in.
She had all the time in the world.
He, she assumed, did not.
Then, without warning, an embarrassing thought surfaced in her mind.
’...Wait.
Why am I waiting for him?’
She blinked.
For the first time in centuries, confusion overtook her.
An instant later, a faint blush quietly spread across her flawless cheeks.
She froze.

chapters.title: Chapter 329: Beyond Earth’s Laws
paragraphs: Although the teleportation itself was instantaneous, Stan had sensed something was wrong before it happened.
Back in the cave, for the briefest fraction of a second, he had felt an indescribable distortion ripple through the space around him. It was subtle enough that he dismissed it as his imagination.
Then it happened again. This time, the feeling intensified.
The air itself seemed to twist, while the world around him folded inward as though reality had suddenly become a sheet of paper being creased by an unseen hand.
By the time he realized something was happening, it was already too late.
An overwhelming force seized him. The strangest part of it all was his System’s complete silence.
No warning. No notification. No attempt to resist.
It was as though whatever was acting upon him possessed an authority that even the System chose not to challenge.
The next instant, he was violently dragged through what felt like countless layers of warped space.
Each layer shimmered with a different color. Black, white, crimson, azure, gold, violet.
Colors he couldn’t even name flashed past in less than a nanosecond each, blending into an incomprehensible stream of light.

With every layer he crossed came the unnerving sensation that his body was being simultaneously disassembled and reassembled, not painfully, but so completely that, for an instant, he couldn’t tell whether he was still the same person emerging on the other side.
Then, as abruptly as it had begun... It ended.
He slammed onto cold, black stone.
He hit the ground on his hands and knees.

The impact sent a jolt through his tempered body. His palms scraped against a surface unlike any stone he had ever touched. It wasn’t the polished chill of marble or the coarse roughness of granite. This was something denser, older. The black stone beneath him possessed a strange mineral composition that he couldn’t identify, and its smooth surface carried a faint, almost wax-like texture, as though it had been shaped by something far more deliberate than the passage of time.
He slowly pushed himself to his feet. The first thing he noticed wasn’t his surroundings.
It was the temperature. The air was... warm.
The realization struck him immediately.

Only moments ago, he had been standing in the frozen depths of Antarctica, enduring relentless polar winds and the icy chill of a glacial cave. Yet now, the air surrounding him felt as gentle as a spring afternoon.
His breath no longer condensed into mist. The cold that had clung to his skin had completely vanished.
There was no doubt about it. He was no longer in Antarctica.
Just then, a series of degraded notifications flickered across his vision.
[Warning.]
[Unknown Spatial Domain detected.]
[Spatial Lock detected.]
[Host is advised to remain on high alert.]
Stan frowned as he read the messages. The System was still functioning. It could still communicate with him.
But something was different.
The notifications lacked their usual precision, appearing clipped and incomplete, as though the System itself had lost access to resources it normally relied upon.
He frowned. "Spatial Lock...
’Doesn’t that mean abilities related to spatial manipulation are being restricted?’
’...That’s bad.’
Taking a slow breath, he tested the theory. ’System. Can I still access my inventory?’
[Inventory functional.]
[Access confirmed.]
’...Phew.’ Relief washed over him.
With a thought, the Introduction to Earth materialized in his hand.
The familiar book felt reassuringly solid. A moment later, he willed it back into storage, and it vanished without issue.
’So the inventory itself was unaffected. Good.’
Next, he attempted something more important.
He reached for the familiar sensation that had once saved his life against the werewolves, willing his own body into the inventory.
Nothing happened. A notification appeared.
[Spatial Lock detected.]
[Host cannot enter Inventory under current conditions.]
Stan’s expression darkened. The System’s answer was simple, clear and final.
Whatever force governed this place had sealed off spatial movement.
He could freely store and retrieve objects from his inventory, but using it as a refuge, or as a means of transportation, was impossible.
In other words... He was trapped.
Letting out a slow breath, Stan straightened to his full height.
Only then did he finally turn his attention to his surroundings.
He wasn’t inside a cave. That was the first realization.
The space around him was simply too vast.

Nothing about it resembled a cavern, a tunnel, or any underground chamber his mind could classify as enclosed. The sheer scale defied comparison. He stood upon the edge of a broad stone ledge, and beyond it...
An entire world stretched before him. Drawn by equal parts curiosity and disbelief, Stan walked to the precipice.
Then he looked out. His breath caught.
Below him, extending all the way to a horizon so distant it seemed impossible for anything beneath the Earth’s surface, lay an immense landscape.
It wasn’t merely a valley. It wasn’t a hidden ecosystem. It felt like an entire continent.

Endless plains rolled into ancient forests. Towering mountain ranges pierced the distance, while winding rivers carved their way across the land. Far beyond, where the terrain finally met the limits of his vision, he could make out what appeared to be a coastline.
Beyond that... A sea.
The landmass continued past the horizon, so immense that he couldn’t even begin to estimate its true size.
Slowly, almost mechanically, Stan lifted his gaze.
There was no sky. Instead, suspended high above the world, floated a colossal crystal.
It was incomprehensibly enormous, dozens of miles across at the very least.
Its body consisted of countless interlocking geometric planes, many still pristine, while others had fractured into intricate fault lines that spread across its surface like glowing veins.
A soft azure radiance emanated from within it. Neither harsh nor dim.
Just enough to bathe the entire world below in an endless, tranquil daylight.
A sun that would never rise. A sun that would never set. The crystal was the sky.
Beneath it drifted floating islands.
Some were only a few hundred meters across, lazily orbiting through the air.
Others were far larger. City-sized.
Even from this distance, Stan could distinguish faint outlines of buildings, roads, and what appeared to be movement.
People... perhaps. Or something else. His attention shifted downward again.
Rivers meandered through the landscape. Then his eyes narrowed. One of them... Was flowing upward.
A tributary climbed from a lower elevation toward a higher one, its waters ascending against gravity in a slow, steady current, as though such a thing were perfectly natural.
For several long seconds, his mind refused to accept what his eyes were seeing.
Then he noticed another. A broad river flowed horizontally across the face of a mountain, moving parallel to the horizon instead of descending toward the valley below.
Gravity itself seemed to have become little more than a suggestion.
Stan slowly turned his attention toward one of the distant peaks. He froze. The mountain... Was upside down.
Its broad base was anchored high in the air, while its jagged summit pointed toward the earth below.
By every law of physics he had ever known, it shouldn’t have existed.
And yet... There it was.
Hanging effortlessly above the world, as though reality itself had decided that "down" was merely a matter of perspective.
Stan stared in silence. After everything that had happened over the past several hours...
After vampires. Werewolves. Qi. Cultivation. Spirit Pools.
His exhausted mind managed only a single, quiet conclusion.
"...This place doesn’t obey Earth’s laws."

chapters.title: Chapter 330: The Hidden Realm
paragraphs: He turned slowly, taking in the full sweep of the place he was standing in.

The ledge beneath his feet was carved from the same dense black stone as everything around him. Behind him, it ended abruptly at a colossal cliff face that rose vertically for what looked to be nearly a thousand meters before curving inward, following the arc of an immense boundary that enclosed this entire world.
A realization struck him.
That boundary... ’is this the underside of Antarctica or something?’

He was standing beneath the continent’s ice cap. Somewhere, thousands of meters above him, the polar cave where he had left Camilla still rested within a glacial mountain, which itself sat upon the frozen surface of an Antarctica he could no longer reach.
His gaze drifted across the landscape below. A group of small, dark figures moved through the middle distance. Creatures.

From this far away, he couldn’t make out what they were, only that they were alive. They traveled in an organized formation, their movements deliberate rather than instinctive. He watched as one of them suddenly took flight, gliding through the crystal-lit sky before landing atop one of the drifting islands. It crossed the island in several long, bounding strides before disappearing behind a low structure.
Whatever they were... They weren’t human.
Farther away, another group moved along the banks of a distant river.

Their posture and coordination resembled that of people, yet something about them was unmistakably different. Even from kilometers away, their skin reflected the crystal light in hues no human complexion ever could.
Stan looked back toward the fractured crystal sky.
Then at the inverted mountain. The rivers flowing upward. The floating islands. The impossible sky itself.
A slow breath escaped him.
He had experienced more than enough impossible things over the past two weeks.
None of them had prepared him for this.
He steadied his thoughts with the discipline he had cultivated since the apocalypse began. Panic achieved nothing. Observation cost nothing.
He was in an unknown location.

His system was still functioning, albeit at partial capacity. His inventory remained accessible, but his personal spatial escape had been completely sealed. Inside that inventory were eighty-five thousand liters of Liquid Qi, his pair of daggers, two books detailing the true history of Earth, and enough supplies to survive for weeks.

Under normal circumstances, none of that would have concerned him. Qi had already transformed his body beyond ordinary human limits. He no longer feared freezing temperatures, thin air, or most natural hazards.
Yet none of that changed one simple fact.
He was somewhere he was never supposed to be.
The realm the werewolves had spoken of.
The place the vampires had come from.
The world the vanished races had disappeared to on the Night of Vanishing.
He suspected he was standing inside it.
Or perhaps... Only at its doorstep.
His gaze returned to the vast world stretching endlessly below.
Somewhere down there, or perhaps in the countless regions beyond it, lay the answers to every question the Introduction to Earth had raised.
The vampires. The werewolves. The demihumans. The True Humans.
The races that modern history believed had vanished, when in truth they had simply gone somewhere humanity could no longer reach.
And now... Stan Harrison was here.

Whether he had been brought here on purpose or by accident, whether the spatial lock was temporary or permanent, whether the crystal sky, the inverted mountain, and the floating islands were real or not... none of that changed the fact that he was here.
And if he was here, then he would have to find a way through.
He couldn’t just stand around and do nothing. He had to find his way back.
’Why am I so sure this is that realm, though? I could be wrong... Whatever. No point dwelling on it right now. I need to find my way back... but I don’t even know where to start.’

He rolled his shoulders, tested the weight of his enhanced body, felt the small but steady current of Qi circulating through his newly opened meridians, and took his first cautious step forward along the black stone ledge.
The world below him waited.
The answers, he suspected, waited with it.

Just as Stan began to think this might truly be the world the werewolves and vampires had come from, just as his mind was beginning to accept that the impossible landscape before him was a real place he had somehow arrived in, the space around him folded once more.
The vast continent crumpled inward and disappeared.
A stone hallway took its place.
Stan blinked. ’What the fuck?!’

He was no longer standing atop the high black stone ledge overlooking the world. Instead, he found himself at the entrance of a narrow corridor carved through solid rock. Its walls rose tall and dark on either side, while its far end disappeared into shadow. The floor beneath his feet was the same dense black stone. The air carried the same warm, ambient temperature.
But the world he had been looking at moments ago was gone.
Replaced entirely by this enclosed passage.
He turned sharply.
The ledge behind him had vanished as well.
In every direction, the corridor was all that remained.

His mind processed the sudden shift with the calm discipline of someone who had already accepted that reality here refused to obey common sense. The underground world had felt real. This corridor felt equally real. Somehow, both seemed to exist simultaneously, yet only one revealed itself at a time.

His instincts, honed by everything he had endured over the past twenty-four hours, told him that neither was an illusion. Neither was a hallucination nor a vision. They were two coexisting layers of the same place, and whatever force governed this realm was allowing him to perceive only one at a time.
He trusted that instinct.
Taking a deep breath, he turned toward the corridor. There was no other path forward.
Whatever had brought him here had presented him with only a single choice, and he had no intention of wasting time resisting it.
With a quiet sigh, he stepped inside.

The stone wall felt solid beneath his palm as he let his hand trail across its surface. It was cold. Dense. Its faintly waxy texture was identical to the ledge outside, and he could feel the rough mineral grain scraping gently against his fingertips.
Real.
Yet undeniably...
Strange.

chapters.title: Chapter 331: The Impossible Corridor
paragraphs: Taking a deep breath, he walked forward.

He walked for what felt like several minutes, the corridor unwinding before him with no sign of variation. The walls remained the same height. The floor stayed the same width. The light retained the same low, ambient blue glow, despite having no visible source.
Then he arrived back at the entrance.
He stopped. Slowly, he turned in place.

The corridor stretched out before him once again, in the very direction he had just come from. The same silent stone. The same unchanging walls. The same impossible extension into a distance that should not have existed inside a passage of any reasonable length.
He tried again. This time, he walked farther and and faster.
Several minutes later... He arrived back at the entrance.
’What the fuck is going one?!’ A frown formed on his face.
He turned around and walked the opposite way. This time, he didn’t return to the entrance.
Instead, he emerged in a completely different section of the corridor, where the passage branched into three separate paths, none of which he had seen before. It was a bit strange but he ran.

He ran hard, drawing upon every ounce of his enhanced speed. The martial mastery embedded within his mind guided his movements instinctively, allowing him to execute footwork techniques he had absorbed but never tested at their limits.
He became a blur racing through the corridor, covering what felt like more than a kilometer.
Then... He arrived at the entrance again.
"..." He tried marking the walls.
Using the edge of his fingernail, he carved a deep groove into the stone at the first junction. His enhanced strength bit cleanly into the surface.
He continued walking, keeping an eye out for the mark. It never appeared.
The walls remained perfectly smooth.
When he returned to the entrance and inspected the original wall, the groove had vanished as though it had never existed.
The corridor was rearranging itself faster than he could observe it.
He tried every movement technique his martial mastery offered. Displacement steps. Rapid pivots.
Wall-runs, to see whether vertical movement produced a different response.
Nothing changed. Eventually, with the quiet resignation of a man who had exhausted every clever idea, he decided to try the simplest one.
He punched the wall. The impact was clean. His fist struck the black stone and rebounded.
Not because the stone had resisted.
But because... there was nothing to break. The wall didn’t crack.
It didn’t chip. It didn’t even acknowledge the strike.
He punched again. The result was identical.
For the third strike, he committed everything..The same fist that can shatter solid steel dumbbells less than a day ago shot forward with the force of a speeding truck.
The instant it connected, a strange sensation washed over him.
It felt as if it wasn’t that the wall had blocked the punch.
It was as though his fist had never actually struck the wall at all. He could touch the wall without issue. He could feel its cold, waxy surface beneath his palm.
Yet the moment he threw a punch... It felt as though the wall ceased to exist, replaced instead by an invisible layer of space itself.
It was an indescribably strange feeling.
Frowning, he stepped back and considered it.
He was about to try a different approach when something caught his eye.
His last strike, the strongest one, had produced a faint distortion in the air around the point of impact.
A ripple. Barely visible but It spread outward through the space before fading almost immediately.
He had missed it before because he’d been watching the stone instead of the air.
He punched again. The ripple appeared once more. Slightly larger this time.
It lingered for a fraction of a second longer before disappearing.
His thoughts immediately connected the pieces.
’The wall isn’t indestructible... Space itself is.’
’The stone is just a manifestation. This corridor is a spatial construct, and it repairs itself faster than I can damage it.’
’I’m not fighting the wall.’
’I’m fighting the space.’
The realization sharpened everything. He had two choices.
He could continue wandering this corridor indefinitely, trapped in loops that would never lead anywhere, slowly exhausting himself against a maze designed to defeat conventional navigation.
Or...
He could strike hard enough that the repairs couldn’t keep up.
Taking a slow, steady breath, he opened the System Shop.
The shop’s combat category had expanded since his last visit.

He scrolled through the offerings with rapid, focused attention. He was looking for a fist technique. Something that could multiply the force of his existing strikes enough to overwhelm the spatial construct’s rate of repair.
He found it three items down.
[Qi Detonation Art]

[A striking technique that channels the practitioner’s stored Qi into the fist and detonates it at the moment of impact. Amplifies the force of a single strike by a factor of ten to fifty, depending on the practitioner’s Qi purity and control.]
[Cost: 7 System Points.]

He willed the purchase. The technique flowed into his mind in the same clean, orderly wave as every other System-granted skill. Its knowledge settled effortlessly into place. The Qi circulation pathways. The compression method. The precise moment of detonation. The intricate routing required to condense and release Qi at the instant of impact.
He closed his eyes and ran through the technique in his mind.

Understanding it, he immediately circulated the Qi flowing through his newly opened meridians. He drew in the faint ambient traces lingering within the corridor and merged them with the reserve already moving through his body.
Then he guided it all into his right fist. The density increased.
Pressure gathered around his knuckles, growing heavier and heavier until his entire arm trembled under the concentrated force.
Without hesitation... He punched.
BOOM!!
The corridor shook violently. At the instant his fist connected, the compressed Qi detonated.
The explosion of force surged through his knuckles, punching not merely into the stone, but through it.
The wall fractured. It truly fractured. Black stone splintered outward as a massive spiderweb of cracks spread nearly three meters in every direction.
More importantly... The air itself cracked.
The faint ripple he had noticed during his earlier attempts had transformed into an unmistakable fracture in space.
A jagged, glowing line of distortion spread outward from his fist, racing across the wall, climbing through the ceiling, and extending into the floor beneath him.
He watched the corridor struggle to repair itself. The cracks in the stone began to close.
The stone healed. The fracture in space did not.
He wasn’t about to let the opportunity slip away. Gritting his teeth, nearly cursing aloud, he struck again.
BOOOM!!
The second blow landed on the exact same spot. The spatial fracture widened.
It spread farther, racing down the corridor in both directions, branching across the ceiling in glowing, jagged lines as the darkness behind the construct became visible through the widening cracks.
He struck a third time.
BOOM!!
The corridor shattered like glass. Every wall. Every section of floor. Every inch of the ceiling. Every enclosed surface of the passage exploded apart simultaneously.
The entire spatial construct fragmented into countless shimmering shards before dissolving into nothingness, the illusion of the corridor collapsing around him like a mirror struck by a hammer.

chapters.title: Chapter 332: Rift Wolves!
paragraphs: The entire spatial construct fragmented into countless shimmering shards before dissolving into nothingness. The illusion of the corridor collapsed around him like a mirror struck by a hammer.
Behind it lay the real path.
Stan slowly straightened, breathing heavily, his fist still raised, then he looked around.

He was standing in a much larger chamber now. The corridor had merely been an enclosure imposed upon a room that had always been three or four times its true size. The actual chamber stretched far into the distance, its walls barely visible. The ceiling soared high overhead. At the far end, a broad passage led deeper into whatever place he had, apparently, been trying to reach all along.
His gaze dropped to his fist.
His knuckles were scraped and slightly bloodied, but the strike had accomplished exactly what he had needed it to.
Yet he also knew... The blow had not been entirely his own.
His current strength should never have been enough.

He was only at the Initial Stage of the Genesis Realm. His Qi reserves were still shallow. Even with the amplification provided by the Qi Detonation Art, the combined force of his attack should not have been capable of fracturing space itself.
Something within the corridor, or perhaps within the very architecture of this place, had allowed the barrier to break.
His strike had merely been the trigger. Not the cause. Someone had been watching. Someone had allowed him to succeed.
’I know you’re watching... Stop playing with me.’ He waited.
Silence lingered for several breaths. Just as he was about to speak again, a voice echoed throughout the chamber.
It came from nowhere. It carried no discernible direction, no accent, no age, no gender.
Rather than traveling through the air, it seemed to resonate directly within his consciousness.
"Good."
Stan spun around instinctively, searching for the speaker, but there was no one.
"Space deceives the weak." The voice paused. "But overwhelming power can shatter deception."
Another pause followed before it spoke once more; "Remember that."
Stan frowned. "Who are you? Are you the one who brought me here? What do you want?"
The cold, detached voice sounded almost amused.
"Patience, kid... Patience."
Stan’s expression tightened. "I know I didn’t accomplish that with my own strength. You helped me. So why bring me here? What is this place? And why are you helping me?
A long silence followed. Finally, the voice answered. "This is an inheritance and I am not helping you, You have merely learned what the corridor was created to teach."
’An inheritance?!’ Stan’s heart skipped a beat.
Even so, he forced himself to remain composed, letting out a dry laugh. "That’s incredibly vague. So the lesson is that brute force breaks space? Why would you want me to learn something like that?"

The voice answered calmly. "Brute force breaks space only when one possesses enough of it. If your strength is insufficient...understanding becomes your only weapon. And understanding is precisely what the corridor exists to teach."
Stan fell silent. His eyes narrowed as he replayed every moment inside the corridor. The walls absorbing his earlier strikes.
The faint ripples in the air he had initially overlooked.
The increasingly visible fractures after each successive attempt.
And finally... The last punch that had shattered the illusion itself. It had never been a maze. It had been a lesson, or to put it simply it was both.
A carefully constructed teaching mechanism that had forced him, through repeated failure, observation, and adaptation, toward a single realization.
Everything he had been trying to destroy was only a projection.
The true foundation had always been the space beneath it.
The voice spoke once more. "Power accomplishes what understanding cannot. Understanding accomplishes what power cannot. The truly invincible possess both."
Stan stood motionless. The meaning settled deep within him. Not merely as knowledge... But as instinct.
He felt something click inside his mind. His perception expanded.

The chamber no longer felt like a simple room enclosed by walls. Instead, it became a three-dimensional region defined by the emptiness between those walls. For the first time... He could perceive space itself. Its subtle texture, Its invisible density. The gentle flow of ambient Qi drifting through it. And beneath it all... The faintest traces of Void.
An endless absence woven through existence itself like invisible threads supporting reality.
At that very moment, the system responded.
[Comprehension of Space acquired.]
[Comprehension of Void acquired.]
[Comprehension of Space: 5%.]
[Comprehension of Void: 1%.]
[Affinity with Space: 5%.]
[Affinity with Void: 1%.]
’So that’s what he was trying to show me...’
’I understand now.’ Stan lifted his head and looked toward the wide passage at the far end of the chamber.
The mysterious voice remained silent.
Without another word, he walked forward, disappearing into the passage beyond.
The next chamber contained the first of the guardians. They were not ordinary beasts.

The first to emerge were four sleek, gray creatures, vaguely wolf-shaped, yet possessed of an unnatural stillness that made them seem wrong even when standing motionless. Their fur shimmered faintly, distorting the air around them, while their pale-blue eyes glowed with an eerie intelligence.
Then they moved. Or rather... They disappeared.

Each wolf vanished from its position and reappeared several meters closer in a single, discontinuous jump. There was no acceleration. No blur of motion. No transition between one point and the next. It was as though the distance separating them from Stan simply ceased to exist.
His mastery recognized the phenomenon instantly.
’I should call them Rift Wolves. Since they’re short-range spatial displacement predators.’
He barely had time to summon Bloodfang from his inventory before the first wolf materialized at his flank. He was barely able to intercept the attack...
A claw still tore across his ribs, leaving a shallow wound that burned far more fiercely than its depth should have allowed. Reacting on instinct, he drove his right-hand dagger forward.
Bloodfang slid effortlessly through the wolf’s throat, meeting the same unnervingly little resistance it had against the polar bear.
The beast died instantly. The remaining three appeared around him in the very same heartbeat.
The next several minutes were brutal.
Stan fought with everything he had. Every parry, every counter, every step was guided by the mastery etched into his mind. He wasn’t fighting creatures that crossed space.
He was fighting creatures that ignored it. They simply materialized wherever the battlefield favored them.

He was wounded again and again. A slash opened his left forearm. A bite passed within a hand’s breadth of his throat. A claw ripped through his thigh deeply enough that every subsequent step sent pain lancing through his leg.
Still... He endured. One wolf fell. Then another. Then the third.

chapters.title: Chapter 333: Guardians Of Space!
paragraphs: Still... He endured. One wolf fell. Then another. Then the third.

With every exchange, his understanding deepened. He stopped trying to follow their movements and instead focused on the fabric of space itself. The instant before each displacement, he sensed the faint disturbance left behind by the collapsing distance.
It was only a fraction of a second. But that fraction was enough. The final Rift Wolf lunged.
But Stan was already moving.
Both Bloodfangs crossed in a crimson arc, one deflecting the beast’s claws while the other pierced straight through its heart.
The wolf collapsed.
"Finally." Stan dropped to one knee, drawing ragged breaths as the adrenaline slowly ebbed from his body.
Only then did the voice return. "Clever. I thought I would have to guide you like last time."

Stan let out a dry scoff between shallow breaths. "Come on. It’s pretty obvious this is all connected. I have to use what I’ve learned to hurt beasts I couldn’t have fought otherwise. What was I supposed to do? Swing a normal sword harder?"

The voice chuckled, sounding genuinely pleased. "Don’t worry. These beasts are all in the same realm as you. Their techniques haven’t fully matured yet. As long as you don’t get reckless, you should be able to handle them."

Stan noted, almost absently, that the voice spoke to him with a warmth that suggested he was not considered an enemy. Ever since the endless corridor, he had been quietly piecing together a working theory of its motives.
So far, every observation pointed toward the same conclusion. The voice had possessed countless opportunities to kill him over the past hour. It had chosen not to.
At the very least, that suggested a neutral relationship. He still didn’t lower his guard. Neutral did not mean trustworthy.
The voice could decide, at any moment, that he had outlived his usefulness.
He remained alert as it spoke again. "The next guardian is coming."
A brief pause followed. "Try not to die, kid."
A faint amusement colored the final words. "I promise you... the gains will be worth it."
The next chamber held a single beast.
It was a mantis.

Over two meters tall, its body was a pure, light-devouring black that seemed to swallow the ambient glow around it. Its blade-like forearms were raised in a poised striking stance, long, curved scythes that shimmered with the same spatial distortion the Rift Wolves had possessed.
"Void Mantis," the voice said softly before falling silent once more.
Stan’s mastery immediately began analyzing it.

Its scythes did not simply cut flesh. They severed distance itself. With a single swing, the space between the mantis and its target collapsed, allowing the blade to arrive instantly regardless of how far away the target had been a heartbeat before.
Stan understood the principle before he even stepped into the chamber.
And he used that understanding against it.

He fought with a refined variation of the technique that had brought down the Rift Wolves. He no longer reacted to the visible strike. Instead, he read the space itself, sensing the subtle distortion gathering around the mantis’s scythes before they moved. He dodged the collapse of distance rather than the blade that followed.
Even so, he was struck twice.
Either blow would have killed an ordinary cultivator. His tempered bones endured.

Meanwhile, Bloodfang drank eagerly. Every time the mantis’s razor-sharp limbs scraped against the crimson blades during a block, tiny traces of its blood were absorbed. With each exchange, the twin daggers grew noticeably warmer in his hands, their faint hum deepening ever so slightly.
Stan waited.
One mistake.
One opening.

It came when the Void Mantis committed to a killing strike. As one scythe carved through empty space where his head had been a fraction of a second earlier, Stan slipped through the gap created by the collapsing distance and drove Bloodfang straight through the center of its body from behind.
The blade burst through its chest.
The Void Mantis shuddered once before collapsing in silence.
The next guardian came without warning. A ripple spread across a shallow pool of still water at the edge of the chamber.
Something rose from within. A serpent, nearly four meters long, its scales smooth as polished obsidian, slithered onto the stone floor. The instant its body fully emerged, it vanished.
A heartbeat later, it appeared within the reflective sheen of the chamber’s ceiling.
Then in the glossy surface of a nearby stone pillar.
Then, to Stan’s surprise, within the blackened surface of one of his Bloodfangs.
"Mirror Serpent," the voice murmured before falling silent once again.
Stan narrowed his eyes. The serpent wasn’t moving through space. It was moving through reflections.

Every polished surface in the chamber became a gateway. It could strike from the reflection in his own dagger, from the faint sheen of the stone walls, or even from the thin puddles of blood scattered across the floor.
There was no safe direction. Only safe moments.

Stan fought with deliberate precision. Every reflective surface within reach was shattered beneath controlled strikes. He kept Bloodfang in constant motion, ensuring neither blade held a clear reflection for more than a fleeting instant. Whenever the serpent lunged from one mirror to another, he tracked the subtle ripple that preceded its emergence instead of the attack itself.
The battle became one of patience.
Then, finally. The serpent emerged from the reflection of a fractured pillar a fraction too slowly.
Stan seized the opportunity.

One Bloodfang slammed its head against the stone floor, pinning it in place before it could retreat into another reflection. The second dagger descended immediately after, driving cleanly through its skull.
The Mirror Serpent convulsed once.
Then its body dissolved into countless motes of black light.

By this point, Stan found himself genuinely relieved that the guardians had faced him one at a time. Had even two of them appeared together, if the Void Mantis had hunted alongside the Rift Wolves, or the Mirror Serpent had shared the chamber with either of them, he would already be dead.
With a thought, he willed the remains of all three guardians into his inventory.
The system accepted them without a sound.
Whatever value their corpses possessed could be examined later.
Exhaling slowly, Stan straightened and turned toward the next passage.

sentences.text: Still...
He endured.
One wolf fell.
Then another.
Then the third.
With every exchange, his understanding deepened.
He stopped trying to follow their movements and instead focused on the fabric of space itself.
The instant before each displacement, he sensed the faint disturbance left behind by the collapsing distance.
It was only a fraction of a second.
But that fraction was enough.
The final Rift Wolf lunged.
But Stan was already moving.
Both Bloodfangs crossed in a crimson arc, one deflecting the beast’s claws while the other pierced straight through its heart.
The wolf collapsed.
"Finally." Stan dropped to one knee, drawing ragged breaths as the adrenaline slowly ebbed from his body.
Only then did the voice return.
"Clever.
I thought I would have to guide you like last time."
Stan let out a dry scoff between shallow breaths.
"Come on.
It’s pretty obvious this is all connected.
I have to use what I’ve learned to hurt beasts I couldn’t have fought otherwise.
What was I supposed to do?
Swing a normal sword harder?"
The voice chuckled, sounding genuinely pleased.
"Don’t worry.
These beasts are all in the same realm as you.
Their techniques haven’t fully matured yet.
As long as you don’t get reckless, you should be able to handle them."
Stan noted, almost absently, that the voice spoke to him with a warmth that suggested he was not considered an enemy.
Ever since the endless corridor, he had been quietly piecing together a working theory of its motives.
So far, every observation pointed toward the same conclusion.
The voice had possessed countless opportunities to kill him over the past hour.
It had chosen not to.
At the very least, that suggested a neutral relationship.
He still didn’t lower his guard.
Neutral did not mean trustworthy.
The voice could decide, at any moment, that he had outlived his usefulness.
He remained alert as it spoke again.
"The next guardian is coming."
A brief pause followed.
"Try not to die, kid."
A faint amusement colored the final words.
"I promise you... the gains will be worth it."
The next chamber held a single beast.
It was a mantis.
Over two meters tall, its body was a pure, light-devouring black that seemed to swallow the ambient glow around it.
Its blade-like forearms were raised in a poised striking stance, long, curved scythes that shimmered with the same spatial distortion the Rift Wolves had possessed.
"Void Mantis," the voice said softly before falling silent once more.
Stan’s mastery immediately began analyzing it.
Its scythes did not simply cut flesh.
They severed distance itself.
With a single swing, the space between the mantis and its target collapsed, allowing the blade to arrive instantly regardless of how far away the target had been a heartbeat before.
Stan understood the principle before he even stepped into the chamber.
And he used that understanding against it.
He fought with a refined variation of the technique that had brought down the Rift Wolves.
He no longer reacted to the visible strike.
Instead, he read the space itself, sensing the subtle distortion gathering around the mantis’s scythes before they moved.
He dodged the collapse of distance rather than the blade that followed.
Even so, he was struck twice.
Either blow would have killed an ordinary cultivator.
His tempered bones endured.
Meanwhile, Bloodfang drank eagerly.
Every time the mantis’s razor-sharp limbs scraped against the crimson blades during a block, tiny traces of its blood were absorbed.
With each exchange, the twin daggers grew noticeably warmer in his hands, their faint hum deepening ever so slightly.
Stan waited.
One mistake.
One opening.
It came when the Void Mantis committed to a killing strike.

As one scythe carved through empty space where his head had been a fraction of a second earlier, Stan slipped through the gap created by the collapsing distance and drove Bloodfang straight through the center of its body from behind.
The blade burst through its chest.
The Void Mantis shuddered once before collapsing in silence.
The next guardian came without warning.
A ripple spread across a shallow pool of still water at the edge of the chamber.
Something rose from within.
A serpent, nearly four meters long, its scales smooth as polished obsidian, slithered onto the stone floor.
The instant its body fully emerged, it vanished.
A heartbeat later, it appeared within the reflective sheen of the chamber’s ceiling.
Then in the glossy surface of a nearby stone pillar.
Then, to Stan’s surprise, within the blackened surface of one of his Bloodfangs.
"Mirror Serpent," the voice murmured before falling silent once again.
Stan narrowed his eyes.
The serpent wasn’t moving through space.
It was moving through reflections.
Every polished surface in the chamber became a gateway.
It could strike from the reflection in his own dagger, from the faint sheen of the stone walls, or even from the thin puddles of blood scattered across the floor.
There was no safe direction.
Only safe moments.
Stan fought with deliberate precision.
Every reflective surface within reach was shattered beneath controlled strikes.
He kept Bloodfang in constant motion, ensuring neither blade held a clear reflection for more than a fleeting instant.
Whenever the serpent lunged from one mirror to another, he tracked the subtle ripple that preceded its emergence instead of the attack itself.
The battle became one of patience.
Then, finally.
The serpent emerged from the reflection of a fractured pillar a fraction too slowly.
Stan seized the opportunity.
One Bloodfang slammed its head against the stone floor, pinning it in place before it could retreat into another reflection.
The second dagger descended immediately after, driving cleanly through its skull.
The Mirror Serpent convulsed once.
Then its body dissolved into countless motes of black light.
By this point, Stan found himself genuinely relieved that the guardians had faced him one at a time.
Had even two of them appeared together, if the Void Mantis had hunted alongside the Rift Wolves, or the Mirror Serpent had shared the chamber with either of them, he would already be dead.
With a thought, he willed the remains of all three guardians into his inventory.
The system accepted them without a sound.
Whatever value their corpses possessed could be examined later.
Exhaling slowly, Stan straightened and turned toward the next passage.

chapters.title: Chapter 334: The Pull!
paragraphs: Exhaling slowly, Stan straightened and turned toward the next passage. He barely managed two steps before a shrill screech tore through the air.

Small, dark shapes materialized from the empty space above him, bat-like creatures whose bodies existed only partially within the visible plane. Half of each creature was here. The other half existed somewhere beyond his sight. Their wings passed effortlessly through the stone walls, and his attacks sliced through them as though they were smoke.
"Abyss Bats." The familiar voice echoed once more. Stan was beginning to find it increasingly annoying.

He gritted his teeth and attacked anyway, but ordinary strikes accomplished nothing. His Bloodfangs passed harmlessly through their partially phased bodies, the blades cutting only empty air as the bats shrieked and swarmed around him in a chaotic dance.
Their attacks were weak. Individually, none of them posed a real threat. Their strength lay in their numbers.
They sought to overwhelm his senses, exhaust his stamina, and slowly wear him down through the accumulation of countless tiny wounds from attacks he could neither predict nor properly defend against.
Stan calmed his mind then he drew upon his newly acquired Comprehension of Space.
Coating one Bloodfang with spatial qi, he struck at the next incoming bat. This time, instead of aiming for its physical body, he targeted the space through which it was phasing.
He willed the dagger to interfere with the phasing itself. The Bloodfang blurred.

The instant it connected, the distorted space around the bat collapsed. The creature was forcibly dragged completely into the visible plane for the briefest fraction of a second, just long enough for the crimson blade to slice cleanly through its body.
The bat let out a piercing shriek before dissolving into black mist.
’It worked!’
"Yes!" A triumphant grin spread across Stan’s face as he repeated the technique on the next bat.

Another died, then another. With each successful strike, the technique became smoother. The first attack had required intense concentration, but every subsequent attempt demanded less effort as his understanding deepened.
Within half a minute, the entire swarm had been exterminated.
The final Abyss Bat gave one last shriek before its severed body dissolved into black mist upon the stone floor.
At that moment, the system responded.
[Comprehension of Space: 10%.]
[Comprehension of Void: 2%.]
[Affinity with Space: 10%.]
[Affinity with Void: 2%.]
Stan straightened slowly, breathing hard. Exhilaration and exhaustion surged through him in equal measure.
He was learning. He was actually, measurably, cultivating. The system’s readouts were not metaphors.

His understanding of space had doubled within the past hour, and with it, his ability to manipulate it. He could feel the difference. The chamber around him had become clearer. The subtle currents of spatial Qi were now visible to his senses, and the underlying structure of the surrounding space had become increasingly legible to his mind.
He was about to celebrate when the voice returned.
"Prepare yourself, kid. What’s coming next is beyond your realm. If I could stop it, I would, but the inheritance decides the trials. All I can do is give you a warning."
Stan’s stomach tightened; "How far beyond?"
"Far enough that you can’t fight it. Don’t even try. Just reach the portal at the other end of this chamber. That’s your only chance."
Stan turned.
At the far end of the chamber, roughly a hundred meters away, a circular portal had materialized in midair, a doorway of softly swirling blue light that glowed steadily against the dark stone walls.
Behind him, the chamber rumbled. Something enormous emerged from the darkness.

At first glance, it resembled a whale. A colossal, sleek-bodied creature of absolute black, it swam effortlessly through the empty air as though the chamber itself were an ocean. Its body stretched well over thirty meters in length.
Its massive fins rose and fell in slow, majestic strokes, propelling it forward with the effortless grace of a creature perfectly adapted to this impossible medium.
Then Stan noticed what followed in its wake. It was not devouring flesh. It was devouring space.
Wherever the whale passed, reality simply ceased to exist. The stone walls vanished. The floor disappeared. Even the air itself was erased.
Everything behind the creature dissolved into an expanding abyss of absolute nothingness, a widening cone of perfect nonexistence that swallowed every trace of reality.
The chamber was not being destroyed. It was being undone.
Every physical thing seemed to disappear, replaced by a void so absolute that Stan’s mind struggled to comprehend it.

He felt the pull immediately. The emptiness left in the whale’s wake was not passive. It actively dragged the surrounding world toward itself, as though reality were desperately trying to fill the impossible absence.
A tremendous force seized his body. His footing slipped.
Within a single heartbeat, his forward movement was cut by more than half as an overwhelming backward pull gripped him.
’Fuck! I can’t die here! What the fuck is this pull?! That bastard didn’t say anything about this!’
The whale’s enormous black eye slowly rolled toward him. Its gaze settled on him. Then its immense jaws began to open.
’Fuck this is bad!’ Stan’s heart skipped a beat. He looked toward the portal.
A hundred meters straight path with no obstacles.
Under normal circumstances, he could have crossed the distance in only a few seconds.
But under this monstrous pull, he needed thirty, at least thirty. But that was the problem, he wouldn’t have thirty seconds.
The whale would consume the very space beneath his feet long before he ever reached the portal.
’Think! Think!! THINK!!’ His mind raced.
His gaze darted between the portal, the whale, and the fabric of space surrounding him.
His final realization in the previous chamber echoed through his mind. He could interact with space itself.
The chamber around him was saturated with ambient spatial Qi, far denser than anything on the Antarctic surface, denser even than the residual Qi leaking from the Spirit Pool.
This place was flooded with spatial Qi. He could feel it permeating the air around him like an invisible ocean.
An idea formed.
’If I can absorb the spatial Qi directly... coat myself in it the same way I coated Bloodfang with it... maybe I can weaken the pull.’
It was the only idea he had. With no better option, he acted.

chapters.title: Chapter 335: Ruins
paragraphs: ’If I can absorb the spatial Qi directly... coat myself in it the same way I coated Bloodfang with it... maybe I can weaken the pull.’
It was the only idea he had. With no better option, he acted.
Drawing upon his newly deepened Comprehension of Space, Stan reached out to the surrounding spatial Qi. Instead of channeling it into his weapon, he pulled it toward his own body.
The ambient Qi flowed across his skin. He compressed it into a thin, dense layer that clung to every inch of his body like a second skin.
The coating resonated with the chamber’s spatial fabric.
Rather than existing as a foreign object within space, his body became, in a localized sense, an extension of it.
Instantly, the pull weakened, not completely but dramatically. Understanding flashed through his mind.

The whale’s devouring force was not targeting living beings. It was consuming space itself. Everything caught within that space was merely dragged along toward the expanding void. This much was pretty obvious.
But by coating himself in spatial Qi that perfectly resonated with the chamber, he had made his body temporarily indistinguishable from the surrounding fabric of space.
To the whale’s devouring field, he was no longer a separate object resisting its pull. He was simply part of the space being drawn forward.
Instead of fighting against the suction, he moved with the surrounding spatial flow, reducing the force acting upon him to only a fraction of what it had been.
At that very moment, the system responded.
[Your Comprehension of Space has increased!]
[Your Comprehension of Void has increased!]
[Comprehension of Space: 15%.]
[Comprehension of Void: 3%.]
[Affinity with Space: 15%.]
[Affinity with Void: 3%.]
With the pull acting on him greatly reduced, Stan ran with everything he had.
He accelerated with every scrap of speed his body could produce. The Qi coating held.

Behind him, the whale opened its jaws even wider and lunged forward. Its great black maw swallowed the space before it in a continuous erasure, closing the distance between them at a terrifying speed.
Stan reached the portal at a full sprint and threw himself through. His body passed into the blue light of the portal...
Behind him, the portal collapsed shut with a single, soundless snap.

The whale’s field of absence, sealed on the other side of the closing portal, could no longer consume its way forward. Stan crashed onto solid stone, rolled several times, then came to rest on his back, gasping for breath.
The ambient Qi coating still clung to his skin. Every muscle in his body burned from the desperate sprint, while the wounds from his previous battles throbbed in protest.
’I made it... I fucking made it!!! I didn’t die?!!’
No words could describe the relief flooding through him.

The sense of death he had felt from the whale was several times greater than what he had experienced against the werewolves. It even surpassed the overwhelming pressure Camilla had once made him feel.
He had never been happier simply to be alive.
Above him, the ceiling of the new chamber glowed with a soft, welcoming golden light.
The familiar voice returned, distant yet unmistakably pleased.
"Well done, kid. You survived the third trial. The rest gets more interesting."
Stan let out a short, breathless laugh before allowing his head to fall back against the stone.
’Fuck you! You’re clearly toying with my life! "More interesting," my ass!’
’Fuck... fuck... fucking hell!!!’

He was beyond annoyed, but there was nothing he could do about it. By now, he had already concluded that the mysterious voice possessed terrifying spatial abilities, making resistance utterly impossible.
Since he had no choice, Stan decided to enjoy the brief moment of peace while it lasted... before asking what the voice meant by "more interesting."
But before Stan could catch his breath, the space around him folded once more.
The gold-lit chamber vanished and he found himself inside a temple.
Or, more accurately, inside what had once been a temple.

The structure lay in ruins. Vast broken pillars rose toward a shattered ceiling. Weathered stone walls, carved with intricate ancient patterns, had been half-eroded by whatever passed for time in this place. Sections of the floor had collapsed into deep, lightless pits. The air was perfectly still. The silence was profound. Whatever had happened here had happened an unimaginably long time ago, and nothing had disturbed the aftermath since.
Beyond the temple’s broken walls, Stan could see the remains of an entire city.

Ruins stretched across the plain in every direction, the skeletons of countless buildings, the faint outlines of streets, and the toppled remains of towering statues that had once stood as monuments to something long forgotten. The sheer scale of the city hinted at a civilization of extraordinary sophistication. Its architecture was unlike anything he had ever seen. The precision of the stonework and the complexity of the carvings suggested a level of craftsmanship that even modern engineering would have struggled to replicate.
And everywhere were bones.
Stan walked slowly into the temple’s central hall before coming to a stop..The floor was carpeted with skeletons.
Not dozens but in thousands.

They lay exactly where death had claimed them, some sprawled across the stone, some frozen in the midst of an attack, others collapsed atop the remains of their enemies. Their bones had been bleached white with age, yet they remained preserved with unnatural perfection. Tattered remnants of robes still clung to many of the skeletons. Around them lay weapons of every kind, swords, spears, staves, bows, and strange artifacts Stan couldn’t even identify.
Stan crouched beside the nearest skeleton and examined it carefully.
The first skull was human. The next skeleton, three paces away, was not. Its cranium was longer, its jaw lined with two prominent canine fangs that remained intact even after death.
’A vampire.’
The next skeleton was unmistakably lupine.
’A werewolf?’

The one beyond it possessed the light, hollow bone structure of what could only have belonged to a hawk-lineage beastkin/demjhumans. Farther ahead lay a fox-lineage beastkin. Then a serpent-lineage one.
Every one of the great vanished races. All of them were here. All of them were dead.
Yet despite their differences, they all shared one thing in common. Most of the skeletons still emanated a faint, lingering pressure.

It was the residual aura of cultivators who had died with immense power still contained within their bodies, the echoes of their strength refusing to fade completely, even after countless ages. Stan’s newly awakened Qi senses perceived those remnants as heavy, cold, and unmistakable.
Even in death, the aura radiating from some of these remains was so overwhelming that they made him seem no more significant than an insect.

chapters.title: Chapter 336: The Price Of Greed
paragraphs: Even in death, the aura radiating from some of the skeletal remains was so overwhelming that it made Stan seem no more significant than an insect.
He straightened and looked across the endless field of bones stretching through the ruined temple.
’This means others reached this inheritance before me,’ he thought. ’And nobody survived.’
The voice, which had remained silent since the golden chamber, spoke once more.
"Are you frightened by their number?"
There was a faint note of amusement in its tone.
The simple question sent a chill racing down Stan’s spine.
By now, he had half expected the voice to speak again, yet hearing it emerge from the silence was no less unsettling.
"Who are these people?" he asked, ignoring the voice’s question entirely knowing the voice is just teasing him...
Anyways, the voice answered without hesitation.

"They are those who came seeking my inheritance and attempted to defy its terms. They sought to circumvent the formation I left behind. They tried to force the trials to yield without earning them. So I used their cultivation as fertilizer to sustain the formation and stabilize this inheritance space."
Stan fell silent for a moment before letting out a low whistle.
"Damn... so they tried to steal your inheritance instead of doing it the normal way."
The voice gave a quiet sigh; "This inheritance was built upon the blood of countless beings. Their number is beyond your imagination."

"I once possessed an infamous reputation. For a time, I stood at the very peak of Earth. Eventually, the world itself became too small for me, so I began preparing this inheritance for a purpose I shall reveal when we meet."
"However, word somehow spread that I had established an inheritance. The strongest cultivators of that era assumed I was nearing death and seeking a successor. Greed clouded their judgment."
"They united to kill me and seize everything I possessed."
A trace of amusement crept into the voice.
"Little did they know that I had already stepped into a realm beyond anything they could comprehend. They never stood a chance."
"I killed them all."
"I used their cultivation as fertilizer to keep this inheritance alive and to power a formation that proved indispensable in accomplishing my goal."
"Because of the uniqueness of that goal, no cultivator was able to enter this place while I slept. Until now.
"You are the first."
"And... you seem rather interesting."
Even at its warmest, even when it openly approved of Stan’s progress through the trials, the voice remained terrifying.
Whatever this existence truly was, it had slaughtered thousands of peak cultivators from the four great races and repurposed their very cultivation to fuel its own domain.
The sheer scale of that massacre dwarfed anything Stan had ever imagined.
"Do not misunderstand," the voice continued calmly. "I am no saint. I have killed more people than you could ever count."
A brief pause followed.
"But every one of them deserved it and it’s for a just cause..."
Stan let out a dry chuckle.
"I don’t really think killing people and using them as fertilizer for your formation qualifies as ’just.’"
The voice sighed again. It was a weary sigh, the kind an ancient teacher would give after realizing a student had misunderstood the lesson.
"You cannot understand with only fragments of the truth."
"But you will."
"Then tell me the whole story," Stan said.
"I will... when you meet me."
"Do not judge the whole from the fragments I have revealed."
"The truth is far more complicated than it appears."
Stan silently filed the answer away. He didn’t press further, after all he was in no position to.

He was a guest, or more accurately, an intruder, inside an inheritance that had killed every other person who had entered it. The voice’s willingness to explain even this much was already more than he had expected. Pushing further would only risk eroding the goodwill he had painstakingly earned.
Without another word, Stan continued deeper into the ruined temple.
Sighing, Stan carefully made his way through the field of skeletons.
He did not disturb them. Nor did he touch the weapons scattered across the floor. Whatever spiritual residue still lingered within those remains was, his instincts warned him, best left undisturbed.
After walking for nearly fifty paces, he began to notice small, floating fragments suspended in the air.

They glowed with a faint radiance. Each was roughly the size of his palm, irregular in shape, drifting lazily at varying heights throughout the ruined temple. They caught the ambient light with a soft, glass-like shimmer, leaving delicate trails of light in their wake as they floated.
Stan stopped before the nearest fragment.

His mastery, still cataloging every unfamiliar phenomenon within this inheritance, failed to identify it immediately. Yet his instincts, honed by everything he had experienced over the past few hours, whispered that these were no ordinary objects.
They were memories. Compressed, preserved. Waiting for someone capable of unraveling them.
Stan slowly reached out. His fingers passed through the fragment without the slightest resistance.
The world around him dissolved. His vision changed.
He was no longer standing inside the temple.

He stood upon a hillside overlooking a landscape unlike anything he had ever seen, a world of impossibly verdant grasslands stretching to a distant horizon, where towering mountain ranges pierced the heavens. Above them, the sky glowed with a warm, golden radiance, as though bathed in an eternal dawn Earth had not witnessed in countless ages.
The air was saturated with Qi. It was so dense that it had become visible, flowing through the atmosphere in slow, luminous misty currents like celestial rivers.
It looked so real that it took Stan a moment to realize he wasn’t truly there, that he was just witnessing.

He had no body within this vision. He was nothing more than a viewpoint anchored to another’s memory, seeing through their eyes, standing where they had once stood, yet unable to move, speak, or alter anything.
Below the hillside lay a magnificent sect.

Its countless buildings rose in elegant tiers of white jade and gold, sprawling across the valley for kilometers. Thousands of cultivators moved through its grounds in disciplined harmony. Some walked along ancient stone paths. Others soared through the skies on their own power. A few sat cross-legged upon floating platforms that drifted effortlessly through the air.
High above the sect, dragons circled. Real dragons.

Long, serpentine creatures whose jade-and-gold scales shimmered beneath the sunlight. Two of them plunged through a sea of clouds, weaving around one another in what was unmistakably playful flight rather than combat.
Stan’s viewpoint shifted.
Time surged forward. The memory unfolded in scattered fragments.
He stood upon another hill overlooking a vast battlefield.

chapters.title: Chapter 337: The Eternal Witness
paragraphs: He stood upon another hill overlooking a vast battlefield.
An army of human cultivators stretched as far as the eye could see, their armor radiating an inner brilliance as their weapons drew streams of Qi from the surrounding heavens.
Facing them stood an equally immense army of vampires.

They wore armor forged from a dark metal that seemed to consume light itself. Crimson eyes burned beneath their helmets like smoldering embers. At the center of their formation sat a regal woman astride a midnight-black warhorse, an ancient crown resting upon her brow.
A queen. The two armies stood in absolute silence. Neither side moved.
It was the suffocating stillness before countless lives were about to collide.
Before the first strike could fall, the memory changed again.
This time... He saw a tree. No. A world tree.

Its trunk alone spanned an entire mountain range, stretching miles across. Its immeasurable canopy blanketed the heavens for hundreds of kilometers, casting a gentle emerald shadow over the land below.
Clusters of radiant fruits hung from its endless branches.
Each fruit overflowed with astonishingly pure Qi, the very essence of cultivation condensed into physical form.
The tree was alive. Not merely living. Aware.
Stan could feel its consciousness. Ancient, vast and patient.
Its thoughts drifted slowly across the world like an endless tide, gently embracing every living thing beneath its branches.
Yet as the memories continued, Stan gradually sensed something else.
An emotion. No... A hatred so profound that it eclipsed everything else.
It did not belong to him. It belonged to the one whose eyes he was borrowing.

Whenever the World Tree entered his field of vision, an overwhelming killing intent surged through the memory. It was so intense that even Stan, merely witnessing the past, felt his heart grow heavy beneath its weight.
And it wasn’t directed at the World Tree alone.
The same boundless hostility extended toward every cultivator he saw, regardless of race or allegiance. Humans. Vampires. Werewolves. Demihumans.
To the owner of these memories, they were all the same.
Stan could only watch in silence. He had no way of knowing why the being harbored such overwhelming hatred for the world before him.
He wasn’t hearing its thoughts. He was only seeing through its eyes.
The memory shifted once more to a sight of War, not just one battlefield but hundreds, perhaps thousands.

The entire world had become a battlefield. Human cultivators led by true humans clashed with vampires. Werewolves tore through ranks of demihumans. Ancient alliances were forged only to shatter moments later beneath betrayal and ambition.
Cities burned. Mountains collapsed. Oceans boiled beneath techniques capable of reshaping the world itself.
The heavens were streaked with countless trails of light as divine artifacts fell alongside the cultivators who wielded them.
It was war on a continental scale. No... On a global scale. The devastation was absolute. Endless wars.
Stan watched them all. Yet something gradually became clear.
The perspective from which he viewed these events was not that of a soldier, a king, or a sect master.
Whoever these memories belonged to had always remained slightly removed.
Watching, observing, and recording. As though history itself were unfolding before an eternal witness.
A question formed in Stan’s mind. ’Whose memories are these?’

When he first touched the fragment, he had assumed it belonged to one of the countless skeletons scattered throughout the temple, a fallen cultivator whose lingering consciousness had left behind fragments of their life. But he couldn’t help but think of these memories are that of the voice.
Unable to contain his curiosity, he asked; "Whose memories are these?"
The voice answered quietly; "Mine."
The memory continued uninterrupted. Nothing within the vision changed. Yet Stan felt his heart tighten.
’Mine.’ The voice was not the lingering remnant of some fallen cultivator.

It had witnessed the Age of Dao with its own eyes. It had watched mighty sects rise. It had watched dragons rule the skies. It had stood beneath the World Tree while it flourished. It had watched civilizations wage wars that engulfed the entire world.
And now... Stan was seeing that forgotten age through the eyes of the being who had witnessed it all.
The memory continued.
The wars faded, the battlefields healed, and new sects rose from the ashes of the old, and new alliances were forged. Peace, fragile yet hard-earned, gradually settled over the world.
Stan watched as the Fourfold Accord described in Introduction to Earth finally came to pass.
Human rulers. Vampire monarchs. Werewolf kings. Demihuman/beastkin sovereigns.
They gathered within a magnificent council hall suspended high above the clouds, where they signed a treaty that would preserve peace for three thousand years.
Stan watched it all unfold. Through the memory, he felt a faint trace of the observer’s emotions.
It wasn’t joy. Nor was it pride. It was a quiet, complicated satisfaction.
The peace had not come easily. It had been earned. And somehow...
The owner of these memories had played a part in making it possible. Then, without warning, everything changed.
The world fell silent. Stan sensed it before he saw it.
The Qi that had saturated the world throughout the entire memory began to thin.
The brilliant currents flowing through the heavens slowed.
Then stopped. Then vanished.
The World Tree’s endless canopy gradually lost its vibrant emerald glow, its leaves turning dull shades of gray, till it was reduced to dust.
High above, the dragons stopped flying. One by one, their silhouettes disappeared from the sky.
In the distance, the great sects dimmed as the formations protecting them failed. The very energy that sustained their existence was abandoning the world.
The Qi was dissapearing...
’The Great Withering.’ Stan was witnessing its beginning with his own eyes.
Yet what unsettled him most was not the collapse of civilization. It was the emotions of the one witnessing it. There was no panic.
No grief. No despair. Only peace. Not the peace of resignation but the peace of fulfillment.

Stan felt it clearly through the memory. The owner of these eyes watched the Age of Dao come to its end. Watched Qi vanish from the world. Watched dragons disappear. Watched entire civilizations crumble. And accepted it all with complete tranquility.
As though everything was unfolding exactly as it was meant to.
As though a plan, nurtured for countless years, had finally reached its conclusion.
Stan’s heart tightened. ’Why...?’
Why would anyone find peace in the death of an entire world?
Unable to suppress the question any longer, he spoke.
"Is this your memory as well?"
The answer came softly; "Yes."
A brief silence followed before the voice continued; "It is also my vision."
"I do not know whether my main body remained here long enough to witness these events before departing elsewhere."
"But I visionised this future."
Stan’s thoughts raced. ’Visionised?’
He forced himself to remain calm as something came to mind; "Does that mean?!"
However, the voice gently interrupted him
